question: Can an iPad show live captions in a lecture?
slides: Captio AI is a full *iPad app.*
Captions in Split View, *beside your notes.*
description: An iPad can show live captions in a lecture or meeting with Apple's built-in Live Captions or with an app made for it, such as Captio AI.
Captio AI is a live captioning app made for deaf and hard of hearing people, and it runs on iPad as a full app in every orientation and window size.
Apple's iOS and iPadOS feature availability page lists 18 language and region entries for Live Captions in November 2026, from Cantonese to Spanish, with no Hindi, Arabic or Polish.
Captio AI captions and translates 60 languages, so a Hindi-speaking student in a lecture hall or a Polish speaker at a conference can read what is said.
Captio AI works in Split View, Slide Over, Stage Manager and resizable windows on iPad, so a notes app can stay open next to the captions.
In landscape on iPad, Captio AI Live Translator shows the original captions and the translation side by side.
Captio AI saves recordings in a searchable library, and you can fix an uncertain word everywhere in a recording with a long press.
Ask the lecturer before you record a lecture, because a saved recording is not the same as reading captions.
Live captions in Captio AI need an internet connection, can contain mistakes, and do not replace a captioner or an interpreter where you are entitled to one.
Captio AI is free to download and the free plan gives 100 free credits a day, as of October 2026.
